'''Oliver Gene Gilbert III''' (born August 15, 1972)<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.legistorm.com/person/bio/487372/Oliver_Gene_Gilbert_III.html |title=Oliver Gilbert - D Florida, 24th, Candidate|publisher=legistorm.com |date=2023 |access-date=2026-10-17}}</ref> is an American politician and attorney who has served as a [[Government of Miami-Dade County|Miami-Dade County Commissioner]] since 2020 as mayor of [[Miami Gardens, Florida|Miami Gardens]] from 2012 to 2020. A [[moderate Democrat]], he is the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] nominee for the [[U.S. House of Representatives]] in [[Florida's 24th congressional district]] in [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Florida|2026]].

==Early life and education==
Oliver Gene Gilbert III was born on August 15, 1972, in [[Miami Gardens]], [[Florida]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Oliver Gilbert |url=https://www.legistorm.com/person/bio/487372/Oliver_G_Gilbert_III.html |work=[[LegiStorm]] |access-date=September 2, 2026}}</ref> Gilbert received a B.A. in Criminal Justice from [[Florida A&M University]] and a J.D. from [[University of Miami School of Law]].<ref name=MDBio>{{Cite web|first= |last= |authorlink   =|title= About Vice Chairman Oliver G. Gilbert, lll  |website=[[Miami Dade County]]|date= |url=https://www.miamidade.gov/global/government/commission/district01/about-commissioner-gilbert.page  |accessdate=April 23, 2021}}</ref> 

==Career==
He entered politics early out of law school in 2000, when then-state representative [[Dorothy Bendross-Mindingall]] hired him as a legislative aide. He then worked as deputy of policy for former US attorney general [[Janet Reno]]'s gubernatorial campaign.<ref name=Scheckner>{{Cite news|date=2020-09-15|first=Jesse |last=Scheckner|title=Oliver Gilbert III: Moving from Miami Gardens mayor to county commission|url=https://www.miamitodaynews.com/2020/09/15/oliver-gilbert-iii-moving-from-miami-gardens-mayor-to-county-commission/|access-date=2020-12-15|newspaper=[[Miami Today]]|language=en-US}}</ref> A couple years later, after working first as a prosecutor and then in private practice, he vied for the mayoralty of the newly incorporated City of Miami Gardens in 2003 where he lost. He was appointed to the Miami Gardens council in 2008 and 4 years later was elected mayor,<ref name=Scheckner/> the second African-American to hold the position. Miami Gardens is Florida's largest city with a [[List of U.S. cities with large African American populations|majority African American population]]<ref name="American FactFinder - Community Facts">{{cite web|url=https://factfinder.census.gov/bkmk/cf/1.0/en/place/Miami%20Gardens%20city,%20Florida/POPULATION/PEP_EST|title=American FactFinder - Community Facts|publisher=United States Census Bureau|access-date=October 22, 2018|archive-url=https://archive.today/20200214005443/https://factfinder.census.gov/bkmk/cf/1.0/en/place/Miami%20Gardens%20city,%20Florida/POPULATION/PEP_EST|archive-date=February 14, 2020|url-status=dead}}</ref> and the [[List of communities in Miami-Dade County, Florida|3rd largest city]] in [[Miami-Dade County, Florida|Miami-Dade County]].

When running for Miami-Dade County Commission he faced Sybrina Fulton, the mother of [[Trayvon Martin]], who was killed by [[George Zimmerman]] in 2013. Although [[Hillary Clinton]], [[Cory Booker]], [[Elizabeth Warren]] and other high ranking figures in the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]] endorsed Fulton,<ref name=Scheckner/> Gilbert won with 50.5% of the vote.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Oliver Gilbert|url=https://ballotpedia.org/Oliver_Gilbert|access-date=2020-12-15|website=Ballotpedia|language=en}}</ref>

===U.S. House of Representatives campaign===
{{See also|2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Florida#District 24}}
Following the retirement of incumbent Rep. [[Frederica Wilson]], Gilbert announced his candidacy for the [[United States Congress]] in June 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |title='I'm running': Oliver Gilbert files for CD 24 race, sets Sunday announcement in Miami Gardens |url=https://floridapolitics.com/archives/800228-im-running-oliver-gilbert-files-for-cd-24-race-sets-sunday-announcement-in-miami-gardens/ |website=[[Florida Politics]] |access-date=September 2, 2026 |date=June 4, 2026}}</ref> He was endorsed for the seat by Wilson, Mayor [[Daniella Levine Cava]], and Mayor [[Eileen Higgins]].<ref name="MH">{{Cite news |last=Habersham |first=Raisa |date=August 18, 2026 |title=Frederica Wilson-endorsed candidate wins primary to fill her South Florida seat |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/news/politics-government/election/article316860168.html |newspaper=[[Miami Herald]] |access-date=September 2, 2026}}</ref><ref name="FP">{{Cite web |last=Scheckner |first=Jesse |title=Shevrin Jones, Oliver Gilbert, Kendrick Meek Jr. lead 7-way Democratic Primary for CD 24 |url=https://floridapolitics.com/archives/813855-shevrin-jones-oliver-gilbert-kendrick-meek-jr-lead-7-way-democratic-primary-for-cd-24/ |work=[[Florida Politics]] |access-date=September 2, 2026 |date=August 17, 2026}}</ref> In the [[primary election]] for the Democratic nomination, Gilbert faced [[Progressivism in the United States|progressive]] state Sen. [[Shevrin Jones]], Kendrick Meek Jr.—son of [[Kendrick Meek]]—and four others.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Scheckner |first=Jesse |date=August 14, 2026 |title='The clear progressive choice': Congressional Progressive Caucus PAC backs Shevrin Jones for CD 24 |url=https://floridapolitics.com/archives/814059-the-clear-progressive-choice-congressional-progressive-caucus-pac-backs-shevrin-jones-for-cd-24/ |work=[[Florida Politics]] |access-date=September 2, 2026}}</ref><ref name="FP"/> During the campaign, Gilbert received criticism from the [[local news|local press]] for attacking Jones for voting in-favor of renaming Palm Beach International Airport to [[President Donald J. Trump International Airport]] after Gilbert approved of renaming a street after [[Donald Trump]] in 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Scheckner |first=Jesse |title=Oliver Gilbert-linked PAC attacks Shevrin Jones over votes for Donald Trump airport renaming |url=https://floridapolitics.com/archives/808771-oliver-gilbert-linked-pac-attacks-shevrin-jones-over-votes-for-donald-trump-airport-renaming/ |work=[[Florida Politics]] |access-date=September 2, 2026 |date=July 21, 2026}}</ref><ref name="FP"/> In August 2026, mass [[text message]]s were sent to residents of the district claiming Jones was [[HIV-positive people|HIV-positive]]; the text were sent from a group impersonating [[Equality Florida]] in "violation of federal law."<ref name="JS">{{Cite web |last=Scheckner |first=Jesse |title='A disgusting attack': Fake Equality Florida text smears Shevrin Jones with false HIV claim |url=https://floridapolitics.com/archives/813116-a-disgusting-attack-fake-equality-florida-text-smears-shevrin-jones-with-false-hiv-claim/ |work=[[Florida Politics]] |access-date=September 2, 2026 |date=August 11, 2026}}</ref> An Equality Florida spokesperson criticized Gilbert and other candidates for their "unwillingness to denounce this smear tactic."<ref name="JS"/> Gilbert later released a statement, saying: "It's a lie. It's evil, hurtful, and it needs to stop."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Bojorquez |first=Manuel |date=August 13, 2026 |title=Florida District 24 candidate Shevrin Jones targeted in false campaign text, causing widespread condemnation |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/miami/news/shevrin-jones-fake-text-district-24-legal-action/ |work=[[CBS News]] |access-date=September 2, 2026}}</ref> On August 18, 2026, Gilbert narrowly won the Democratic nomination, receiving 34.4% of the vote to Jones' 32%.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Candido |first=Sergio |date=August 18, 2026 |title=Oliver Gilbert wins Democratic primary for Florida's 24th Congressional District; Jones concedes |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/miami/news/2026-florida-primary-district-24-oliver-gilbert/ |work=[[CBS News]] |access-date=September 2, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Mancini |first=Ryan |date=August 18, 2026 |title=Gilbert wins Democratic primary for open Wilson House seat in Florida |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/6021111-gilbert-wins-florida-house-primary/ |newspaper=[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]] |access-date=September 2, 2026}}</ref> In the [[general election]], Gilbert is facing [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] nominee Mayonna Te Brown; however, winning the Democratic primary in the 24th district is considered "[[tantamount to election]]."<ref name="MH"/>

==Personal life==
Gilbert loves [[bowtie]]s and frequently wears them.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jazz In The Gardens {{!}} The Mayor of Miami Gardens Talks Jazz in the Gardens, the Birth of the City and His Love of Bow Ties|date=23 January 2019 |url=https://www.jazzinthegardens.com/the-mayor-of-miami-gardens-talks-jazz-in-the-gardens-the-birth-of-the-city-and-his-love-of-bow-ties/|access-date=2020-12-15|language=en-US}}</ref> He is a brother in [[Omega Psi Phi]] fraternity.<ref name=MDBio/>
